text: The elevator stopped between floors, and the lights went out.
Nobody expected the vending machine to start talking.
The wedding cake arrived with a small parachute attached.
At 3 a.m., the hotel phone rang for the third time.
The new neighbour's dog knew exactly where the treasure was buried.
The office printer had finally developed a personality.
The last train of the night was heading the wrong way.
The museum guard noticed the painting had changed overnight.
The camping trip took an unexpected turn when the map began to glow.
The bakery's new pastry had a very suspicious name.
The entire choir forgot the words at the same moment.
The package had no address, only a drawing of a lighthouse.
The weather forecast promised snow, but the sky was full of confetti.
The old radio only played songs from the future.
The restaurant had one table, one waiter, and no menu.
The library book was returned with sand in every page.
The football match was interrupted by a very determined goose.
The new housemate arrived carrying a grandfather clock.
The teacher's chair squeaked in complete sentences.
The road trip playlist suddenly included a recording of the car.
The plant on the windowsill had grown a tiny door.
The office fridge contained a cake shaped like the boss.
The ferry left the harbour with nobody at the wheel.
The neighbours were having a very loud argument about soup.
The theme park ride stopped at the highest point, facing the exit.
The package arrived ten years after it was ordered.
The cat brought home a receipt for something nobody bought.
The last slice of pizza came with a handwritten warning.
The art class was asked to paint the sound of a Monday.
The supermarket announced a surprise guest over the intercom.
The vending machine refused to sell anything except advice.
Every clock in the house stopped at exactly the same second.
The new employee's desk came with a very specific list of rules.
The bus driver announced a detour through a forgotten memory.
A tiny door appeared in the back of the fridge overnight.
The wedding photographer noticed an extra guest in every photo.
The final exam question was a drawing of a closed door.
The neighbourhood cat had started collecting receipts.
The radio station played the same three seconds of a song all day.
The hotel key opened a room that was not on any floor plan.
The bakery sold a loaf of bread with a handwritten apology inside.
The garden gnome had moved again, this time to the roof.
The office plant began dropping notes instead of leaves.
The train stopped at a station that was not on the map.
The cinema screen went dark just as the film revealed the culprit.
The new app promised to predict what you would forget next.
The old lighthouse began flashing a pattern in Morse code.
The pizza delivery arrived with a map to somewhere else.
The school choir was asked to sing a song nobody had heard.
The library's returns bin contained a pair of muddy boots.
The camping stove worked perfectly only when it was raining.
The street musician was playing a song about the people watching.
The parcel had been forwarded through twelve countries and one kitchen.
The dishwasher began leaving messages in the fog on the window.
The football stadium echoed with a whistle nobody had blown.
The art gallery's newest painting was still wet and moving.
The lift button for the thirteenth floor lit up for the first time.
The neighbour's barbecue smoke formed a perfect question mark.
The last ferry of the night had a passenger list with no names.
The museum's dinosaur skeleton was missing one very important bone.
